title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the continuation of the 'Longue Marche' material, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Grothendieck is working with a group of 'operators' u in a group \tilde{Γ}_σ (or \tilde{M}_{0,3}). These act on the profinite fundamental group \hat{Π}_{0,3}, the free profinite group on two generators, and on its variants. To each u are attached elements g(u), h(u), f(u) and α(u), β(u). These play the role of the GT-type data: f is the 'twisting' element, g and h are the analogous elements for the other punctures or symmetric versions.

On the previous page (p.385) the theorem to prove is that φ' = (φ'_0, φ'_σ) is a group homomorphism. Here φ'_σ(u) = μ(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^ξ is a matrix in GL(2,\hat Z) (up to some prime/quotient). Compatibility (9) is built into the construction. What remains is multiplicativity (8a). For this, Grothendieck first records the 'cocycle relations' (10) for g, h, f under composition of operators.

This page does the following.
(i) Remark 1 gives the same twisted cocycle relations (11) for α and β: α(u'u) = u'(α(u))·α(u'), and β likewise.
(ii) Remark 2 notes that f satisfies f(u'u) = f(u')·u'(f(u)), with the factor order reversed relative to g and h. One could make the formulas uniform by replacing g and h by g^{-1}, h^{-1}, as was done earlier with f.
(iii) He pushes all these non-abelian 1-cocycles into SL(2,\hat Z)' (or GL(2,\hat Z)^{±}' for α), keeping the same letters. The twisted action of u' then becomes conjugation by the matrix φ'_σ(u'). This gives (12): each of g, h, α, β satisfies c(u'u) = int(φ'_σ(u'))(c(u))·c(u'), and f satisfies f(u'u) = f(u')·int(φ_σ(u'))(f(u)).
(iv) He stresses the payoff. In GL(2,\hat Z) these relations are completely explicit (four matrix coefficients, so an effective computation is possible). In \hat{Π}_{0,3}, by contrast, quantities like u'(g(u)) cannot be expressed by simple algebraic formulas in the data determining u and u'.

On the next page this becomes f'' = f' u' f u'^{-1}, with explicit 2×2 matrices, μ'' = μμ' and ε'' = εε'. This sets up a direct verification that φ_σ(u'u) = φ_σ(u')φ_σ(u). In modern terms: Drinfeld/Ihara-style composition laws for GT elements (crossed homomorphisms), projected to the 2-dimensional 'linear' level (the action on \hat{Π}_{1,1}^{ab} ≅ \hat Z^2), in order to prove that a matrix-valued map is a homomorphism.
errors: Notational inconsistency in (12): the f line uses int φ_σ(u') while the other lines use int φ'_σ(u'). Presumably the same map is meant.

The ordering for f (f(u')·u'(f(u))) differs from that for g, h, α, β (u'(c(u))·c(u')). This is not an error: Grothendieck explicitly flags it and proposes the inversion g→g^{-1}, h→h^{-1} to make the conventions uniform.
On p.385 the h-relation in (10) carries an uncertain exponent '?'. The derived relations here are only as reliable as that convention.

ideas.what: Composition (cocycle) law for the twisting elements f, g, h attached to automorphisms of the profinite free group of rank 2 (GT-type elements): f(u'u) = f(u')·u'(f(u)).
ideas.modern_name: Multiplication law in \widehat{GT} / non-abelian crossed homomorphism
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated); not in published texts as such

ideas.what: Pushing the non-abelian cocycles into SL(2,\hat Z)/GL(2,\hat Z), where the twisted action becomes conjugation by a matrix φ_σ(u'), giving explicitly computable cocycle relations.
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-cocycles under the map to the action on H_1 of the once-punctured elliptic curve (\hat Π_{1,1}^{ab})
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (GT action on Π_{1,1}, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto style linearizations)

ideas.what: Strategy: verify that a matrix-valued map built from GT-type data is a homomorphism by computing at the GL_2 level, where the composition is algebraically explicit, rather than in the free profinite group.
ideas.modern_name: Linearization / abelianization of the Galois–Teichmüller action

missed.claim: The page records twisted cocycle laws for five data (g, h, f, α, β) attached to a GT-like group element, with an explicit remark on the order convention. These laws are the composition law later made standard by Drinfeld/Ihara for \widehat{GT}, and here they predate those papers in Grothendieck's unpublished work. The content itself is routine.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it documents that Grothendieck had worked out the GT-type composition laws and their GL(2,\hat Z) shadows in detail.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of cocycle relations and their images in GL(2,\hat Z) in preparation for a homomorphism check. It is historically interesting as a precursor of the \widehat{GT} composition law, but mathematically standard.
transcription_corrections: 'On aura d'ailleurs des [?]' probably reads 'On aura d'ailleurs de même'.
'on aurait aussi de changer au cas des notations' is likely 'on aurait avantage à changer un peu les notations'.
'(comme précédemment on qu'était devenu f^{-1} ...)' is likely '(comme précédemment ce qui était devenu f^{-1} ...)'.
In the first line of (11) the image shows 'u'(α(u)).α(u')', consistent with the transcription.
The last lines likely read 'Ces formules dans GL(2,\hat Z)' ont l'avantage d'être des formules entièrement explicites (prémices d'un calcul effectif), contrairement…'.
